posts.text: Five days, three theatres of conflict. US and Iran escalate in Jordan. Russia pounds Kyiv. Argentina claims the Falklands. Canada's fires cross borders. Israel expands settlements. Here's how the map moved this week. a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Two American soldiers killed in Jordan as Iran attacked Muwaffaq Salti Airbase Friday. US retaliated with an eighth consecutive night of strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz—putting the world's most critical energy chokepoint directly in the crosshairs.

2/ Sunday: Russia's heaviest ballistic bombardment of the entire war. ~40 missiles hit Kyiv in five hours. At least one dead, 22 injured. Ukrainian air defences exhausted. This is what happens when one side has cruise missiles and the other runs out of ammunition to stop them.

3/ After Argentina's World Cup semi-final win, players held a banner: 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas.' A 44-year-old dispute—and a 1982 war that killed 900—reignited on football's biggest stage. The South Atlantic's frozen conflict is far from over.

4/ Nearly 200 fires burn in Ontario. Smoke blankets NYC and the north-east. Trump threatened tariffs on Canada. Carney said both nations share climate responsibility. A climate crisis that doesn't respect borders is becoming a trade war.

5/ Israel announced plans for three new outposts in Gaza and $400M+ for West Bank settlement expansion—while already controlling 65% of Gaza. Each expansion deepens occupation and moves a two-state solution further away.

The parallel: Crimea 2014. Russia's first act of post-Soviet territorial seizure. Twelve years later, Kyiv endures the heaviest bombardment since the full 2022 invasion began. Crimea wasn't an isolated provocation—it was the opening move of a war still unfolding today.
